title: No Anthropic Stock Exists, but Crypto Traders Just Priced It at $2T
summary: The artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic is still private, but crypto traders are assigning the Claude maker an implied valuation of about $2.12 trillion through synthetic perpetual contracts that do not represent company shares. The juggernaut OpenAI has witnessed its synthetic perp contrac...
content:
The artificial intelligence (AI) giant Anthropic is still private, but crypto traders are assigning the Claude maker an implied valuation of about $2.12 trillion through synthetic perpetual contracts that do not represent company shares. The juggernaut OpenAI has witnessed its synthetic perp contracts push the firm’s inferred worth to $1.58 trillion.

Key Takeaways

  • Binance is using a 1 billion-share estimate to work out the AI company Anthropic’s implied valuation. At press time, ANTHROPIC stands over $2 trillion.
  • Anthropic warned back in May that unauthorized SPV stock transfers are void and could basically end up being worthless to investors trading or holding these assets.
  • Binance could adjust ANTHROPIC/USDT if the share count in Anthropic’s S-1 comes in 3% or more above or below its current estimate.

On Sept. 9, Defillama’s pre-IPO dashboard showed Binance’s ANTHROPIC/USDT contract testing $2,120. Binance applies an assumed share count of 1 billion, turning that contract price into an implied company value of roughly $2.12 trillion. Similar contracts on Bitget, Kraken, BingX, Aster, and Coinbase International were trading in the same price range.

Crypto Traders Push Anthropic Above Its Last Private Valuation

That figure is more than double Anthropic’s last negotiated private-market valuation. The company raised $65 billion in a Series H round on May 28, valuing Anthropic at $965 billion after the financing round.

Late August had already been a wild ride. ANTHROPIC/USDT traded around $1,600 to $1,840 on Binance-tracked markets, implying roughly $1.6 trillion to $1.84 trillion under the same 1 billion-share assumption. A Hyperliquid market deployed by Entropy briefly printed above $2 trillion and settled near $1.97 trillion around Aug. 28.

The catch is that none of those contracts are Anthropic stock. Binance listed ANTHROPIC/USDT on June 2 as a USDT-margined perpetual contract with up to 20 times leverage. It settles in tether and uses a market price created by trading on the exchange, not a public share price.

A $2 Trillion Ticker Is Not the Same as Owning Stock

Binance says its 1 billion-share estimate is informational only and that any implied valuation is not attributable to or endorsed by the exchange. “If the Pre-IPO Perp is transitioned to a TradFi Perp, a Pre-IPO Transition Notice will be issued,” Binance explains on its web portal.

OKX uses a 10 billion-share assumption, producing a lower per-unit quote but roughly the same implied company value. These perpetuals do not put traders on Anthropic’s cap table or deliver shares at settlement. They are derivatives that let traders bet on where they think Anthropic could eventually be valued. Interestingly, the ANTHROPIC ticker can look like a stock quote even though no public stock sits behind it.

A separate product has added more confusion. Prestocks issues an ANTHROPIC token on Solana that claims economic exposure through a special-purpose vehicle, or SPV. On Sept. 9, the token traded around $961 to $973 with a market cap of about $7.1 million to $7.2 million, while the Prestocks’ dashboard showed an implied Anthropic valuation near $1.59 trillion.

Anthropic Warns Unauthorized Investment Structures May Be Worthless

Anthropic has pushed back against that structure. In May, the company said it does not permit SPVs to acquire Anthropic stock, that transfers into an SPV are void and that third parties selling exposure through tokenized securities, forward contracts or similar mechanisms may be offering investments with no value. PreStocks tokens fell roughly 34% to 45% after the warning.

On the flip side, traders do have reasons to speculate. Anthropic’s private-market valuation climbed from $380 billion in February to $965 billion in May, while its annualized revenue run-rate was disclosed near $47 billion at the Series H close and later reported around $65 billion by the end of July.

Bankers and investors have discussed a possible listing in the $1.5 trillion to $2 trillion range. Still, the contracts are tiny compared with the value they imply. Defillama lists more than a dozen Anthropic perpetual markets, while combined open interest on the largest books is only in the tens of millions of dollars.

Alongside Anthropic, OpenAI’s pre-IPO shows the OPENAI/USDT contract traded around $1,578 on Sept. 9 on Binance, and on Kraken, OpenAI pre-IPO assets swapped hands for $1,604. Prestocks shows OpenAI tokens at $1,084 and a $1.34 trillion implied market cap. Like Anthropic, OpenAI has disclosed confidentially with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) that it planned to go public.

The IPO Will Test Crypto’s $2 Trillion Bet

For now, anyone reading ANTHROPIC/USDT, or any pre-IPO contract or token, as a true equity price is playing with fire. Binance says it will rescale the contract if an amended S-1 shows a share count that differs from its estimate by 3% or more.

That makes the eventual IPO the reality check. Until registered shares are actually priced, the $2.12 trillion figure is a leveraged crypto-market opinion on Anthropic’s future value, not a price the company has authorized, sold, or promised investors.

title: Illinois Crypto Tax Faces New Court Bid Before It Hits Residents
summary: Illinois’ 0.2% digital asset tax could cost crypto firms millions and expose them to felony charges for compliance errors, two trade groups warn. They want enforcement blocked before the Jan. 1, 2027 launch produces irreversible costs and customer losses. Crypto Groups Race to Stop Tax Before Illino...
content:
Illinois’ 0.2% digital asset tax could cost crypto firms millions and expose them to felony charges for compliance errors, two trade groups warn. They want enforcement blocked before the Jan. 1, 2027 launch produces irreversible costs and customer losses.

Key Takeaways

  • Two crypto groups are seeking a preliminary injunction.
  • The 0.2% tax applies to covered exchanges, transfers, and storage.
  • Plaintiffs say companies face millions of dollars in compliance costs.

Crypto Groups Race to Stop Tax Before Illinois Users Pay

Illinois crypto users could soon owe tax for moving or storing digital assets, even when no sale occurs and no profit is earned. The Crypto Council for Innovation and Blockchain Association filed a preliminary injunction motion Sept. 8 asking the Sangamon County Circuit Court to block the tax before it takes effect Jan. 1, 2027.

The Crypto Council for Innovation advocates for digital asset policies, while Blockchain Association represents more than 100 industry companies. Their request advances an Aug. 21 lawsuit alleging that the tax discriminates against electronic commerce, burdens interstate transactions, denies due process, and violates Illinois constitutional requirements governing taxation and lawmaking.

The organizations argue that unclear rules could cause a single exchange, transfer, and storage sequence to trigger the 0.2% levy as many as three times. They also claim companies are already facing millions of dollars in compliance costs and may lose customers before the court resolves the case. Crypto Council for Innovation CEO Ji Hun Kim stated:

“A ruling that arrives after the tax takes effect does not undo these harms.”

Illinois Tax Reaches Transfers and Storage

The Digital Asset Tax Act, contained in Public Act 104-0468, imposes a 0.2% tax on the value associated with covered digital asset activity received by an Illinois customer. The law encompasses individual occurrences of exchanging, transferring, or storing digital assets through a broker and requires the charge to appear separately from the purchase price.

Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed the budget legislation June 16, while the tax and its registration requirements become operative Jan. 1, 2027. The state expects the 0.2% levy to generate approximately $60 million annually.

Out-of-state brokers generally enter the collection framework after earning at least $100,000 in gross receipts from Illinois digital asset activity during the preceding 12 months. An analysis by international law firm DLA Piper found that brokers must register before conducting covered business, while certain recordkeeping, registration, and filing violations carry Class 3 felony penalties.

For an individual, an Illinois Class 3 felony generally carries two to five years in prison, although probation or another authorized sentence may apply. The law’s criminal provisions include failing to register, filing a fraudulent return, failing to file a return, and failing to maintain required records.

The levy differs from conventional taxes applied to gains or income by using the value of the underlying digital asset as its stated base. Cryptocurrency activity can already produce capital gains and income tax obligations, depending on the transaction, but the Illinois measure separately reaches covered asset exchanges, movements, and storage.

Plaintiffs Cite Unresolved Compliance Questions

The associations argue that the statute leaves companies unable to determine how often an exchange or continuing storage arrangement becomes taxable. Their motion also questions how brokers should establish an asset’s value and resolve conflicting indicators of whether a customer is located in Illinois.

The motion illustrates the potential disparity between the tax and the underlying service fee with an example involving $1 million in digital assets. A broker might charge between $1 and $10 for the service while Illinois collects $2,000 in tax, according to the filing.

The current case is not the first challenge to the measure. The Digital Chamber sued Illinois on July 21, similarly alleging violations of the Commerce Clause, due process protections, the Illinois Constitution, and the federal Internet Tax Freedom Act.

Blockchain Association CEO Summer Mersinger contrasted roughly $60 million in projected tax revenue with more than $224 billion in state appropriations, saying:

“Illinois has enacted a first-in-the-nation tax that unfairly singles out digital commerce, fragments a national market, and exposes companies and ordinary Illinoisans to severe penalties – including felony liability for companies – for guessing wrong about an indeterminate statute.”

The court must now decide whether to block enforcement while the broader constitutional challenge proceeds.

title: Visa Stablecoin Settlement Tops $20 Billion as Card Volume Surges
summary: Visa’s stablecoin settlement volume has climbed above a $20 billion annualized run rate, up more than 15-fold from a year ago. The growth is forcing card issuers, lenders and banks to rethink how they finance settlement in an always-on crypto market. Visa Stablecoin Cards Expand to 160+ Programs Wor...
content:
Visa’s stablecoin settlement volume has climbed above a $20 billion annualized run rate, up more than 15-fold from a year ago. The growth is forcing card issuers, lenders and banks to rethink how they finance settlement in an always-on crypto market.

Key Takeaways

  • Visa stablecoin settlement topped a $20B annualized run rate, with 160+ card programs live.
  • Onchain credit cuts financing costs by up to 30% and enables 7-day card settlement.
  • Visa-linked lenders seek to scale working capital fast enough to match stablecoin card growth.

Visa Stablecoin Cards Expand to 160+ Programs Worldwide

Visa’s stablecoin business is starting to look less like an experiment and more like a new payments rail.

Stablecoin settlement volume on the network has surpassed a $20 billion annualized run rate, more than 15 times the level recorded a year earlier. At the same time, more than 160 stablecoin-linked card programs were live globally in Visa’s fiscal second quarter.

Payment volume across those programs rose nearly 200% year over year.

The headline is not simply that crypto cards are growing. It is that the financial plumbing behind them is beginning to change with them.

Stablecoin Cards Are Creating a New Funding Problem

Every card program has to meet its daily settlement obligation before cardholders repay what they owe.

For large issuers, that gap is usually financed through warehouse lines or securitization. However, many early-stage stablecoin card programs need only a few million dollars at a time. They also settle seven days a week.

That creates an awkward mismatch. Traditional credit facilities can be too expensive and too slow to document for smaller programs that need capital drawn and repaid daily.

Visa said some crypto-linked card businesses are therefore constrained not by user demand, but by access to working capital designed for an always-on settlement cycle.

Credit Coop Brings Settlement Financing Onchain

Credit Coop, working with Visa, has built a stablecoin-denominated revolving credit facility aimed at that gap.

The system uses a smart contract called Spigot to route settlement receivables and automatically service repayments. It is designed to perform a role similar to a traditional lender lockbox, but through code.

Across the platform, more than 9,000 repayments have been executed onchain.

Credit Coop also receives authorized Visa settlement files directly, allowing lenders to compare network data with onchain repayment history. As more lenders have become comfortable with the structure, borrowing costs for participating programs have fallen by as much as 30%.

$2.5 Billion Financed With Zero Defaults

The strongest proof point so far comes from Rain, a Visa Principal Member that has used Credit Coop to fund daily settlement since August 2023.

Across its platform, Credit Coop says it has financed more than $2.5 billion in cumulative volume, processed over 3,000 borrow events and 9,000 repayments, with zero defaults.

Karta later used the same model while building its credit history before securing a $125 million institutional credit facility as part of a larger $140 million financing package. That progression matters for banks and lenders.

Stablecoin-linked cards are not only expanding crypto payments. They are also creating a new class of receivables-backed credit that can be monitored and serviced in real time.

For Visa, the $20 billion run rate is significant because it shows stablecoins are moving deeper into mainstream payment infrastructure. The next growth bottleneck may not be adoption. It may be financing the settlement layer fast enough to keep up.

title: Cut off From Global Finance, Iran Turns to Bitcoin and Tether
summary: According to reports, cryptocurrency use in Iran is not fringe but a working trade-settlement rail. Tehran is quietly moving funds across these digital rails using bitcoin (BTC) and tether (USDT) to undermine financial sanctions. Digital Assets Take on a Bigger Role in Iran’s Trade On Wednesday, the...
content:
According to reports, cryptocurrency use in Iran is not fringe but a working trade-settlement rail. Tehran is quietly moving funds across these digital rails using bitcoin (BTC) and tether (USDT) to undermine financial sanctions.

Key Takeaways

  • Iran’s crypto activity hit roughly $10 billion in 2025 as trade is increasingly moving onchain in 2026.
  • CCAF puts Iran at 0.12% of global bitcoin hashrate, far below Elliptic’s 4.5% estimate.
  • Bessent’s Aug. 24 Operation Economic Outcast puts Iran’s crypto channels in the crosshairs.

Digital Assets Take on a Bigger Role in Iran’s Trade

On Wednesday, the Financial Times (FT) reported that Iran’s central bank has told businesses and traders to repatriate funds by any means necessary, including using bitcoin and tether. FT reporter, Najmeh Bozorgmehr, based in Tehran, cites “Iranian businesses, regime insiders and analysts” who are familiar with the matter.

FT reports that $10 billion in cryptocurrency moved through Iran in 2025, while its analysis also cites blockchain analytics firm Elliptic, which estimates that Iran accounts for 4.5% of global bitcoin mining hashrate. Bitcoin.com News independently checked both figures and found that the $10 billion estimate originates from TRM Labs and Chainalysis, two blockchain analytics firms that placed Iran-linked cryptocurrency activity between $8 billion and $10 billion.

Elliptic’s mining estimate is less clear-cut, however, as several other sources place Iran’s share of global bitcoin hashrate considerably lower. Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance (CCAF) shows Iran’s measure of the global hashrate stands at 0.12%, and hashrateindex.com’s hashpower heatmap has Iran sitting at around 0.2% in Q3 2026. However, CCAF leverages an IP method to get its count, and it can be perceived as an undercount because Iranian miners can use VPNs.

Crypto Takes Root as Iran Pushes Against U.S. Sanctions

This is not the first time reports have said Iran has been leveraging bitcoin and stablecoins during the war against the United States. In April, it was reported that Iran was charging cryptocurrencies and stablecoins for safe passage through the Strait of Hormuz. In June, Bitcoin.com News reporter Sergio Goschenko covered how Iran was charging $2 million per vessel in BTC and USDT.

Alongside this, former Central Bank of Iran PR chief Mostafa Ghamari Vafa posted on X in April and said that the central bank opened four special accounts. He said one account was for the rial, with others for the yuan, the U.S. dollar, and the euro. The accounts were made specifically for Hormuz transit fees collected by the IRGC Navy. The former PR chief, however, did not mention bitcoin or tether in his statement at the time.

Bozorgmehr’s report says that Iran’s judiciary estimates there’s a lot of undeclared earnings at home and overseas from importers and exporters, roughly $100 billion. “Receiving cryptocurrencies for exports is now totally established,” an Iranian business executive told the FT reporter. FT reached out to the country’s central bank, and representatives declined to comment.

Washington Targets Iran’s Growing Digital Asset Channels

Back in May, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent revealed at the Reagan National Economic Forum in Simi Valley, California, that the department had seized roughly $1 billion in cryptocurrency assets tied to Iran. Just recently, Bessent warned foreign nations to sever Iranian digital asset ties, and Bessent told the press that a plan called Operation Economic Outcast would push that goal. It was formally launched on Aug. 24.

Bozorgmehr also discussed the alleged crypto activity with a member of the Iran Digital Transformation Association. This particular member noted that the central bank “no longer insists” on enforcing hard rules against bitcoin trading platforms. FT’s report and the others before it, published this past spring, signal the fact that financial sanctions are losing their sting in a borderless digital era.

title: Solana Price Prediction: SOL’s Monthly Momentum Flips as Bulls Target $120 and $146
summary: Solana price is trading near $103 after a strong recovery, with bulls now watching key support levels and the next major resistance targets.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: SOL

Solana price is trading near $103 after a strong recovery, with bulls now watching key support levels and the next major resistance targets.

The higher-timeframe picture is also shifting, with monthly momentum indicators improving after an extended bearish period. Solana is trading near $103.47 after slipping around 0.18% over the past 24 hours, according to Brave New Coin data.

Beyond price action, Solana continues to expand its role in tokenized real-world assets. The network reportedly handled $14.7 billion in tokenized asset trading over the past year, providing a fundamental backdrop as traders focus on $120 and $146 as the next major technical levels.

Solana Indicators Point to a Major Momentum Shift

Solana price has recorded its first green monthly candle in ten months after a strong recovery from the recent low around $60. The move alone does not confirm a full trend reversal, but it marks a notable change after months of persistent selling pressure. The momentum picture is also improving. Ash Crypto highlights that the monthly MACD is approaching a bullish crossover, while monthly RSI has broken above a descending trendline that had remained intact for roughly two years. Both developments suggest the larger bearish momentum structure may be starting to weaken.

If the MACD crossover confirms while SOL continues holding above $100, the combination would add weight to a longer-term recovery. The next challenge is translating those improving monthly indicators into sustained price acceptance above the resistance levels sitting between $120 and $146.

Solana has printed its first green monthly candle in ten months as MACD approaches a bullish crossover and RSI breaks a two-year downtrend. Source: Ash Crypto via X

Solana Facing Next Resistance at $120

The daily chart has already produced one important technical change by breaking above the $97.70 resistance level. SOL price is now trading around $103-$105, leaving the former resistance zone as the first important support beneath price.

The setup highlighted by Ucan Coin places $120.23 as the next major resistance. A sustained move through $120 would confirm another higher high and could extend the recovery towards the larger $146.56 level.

SOL has broken above $97.70, with $120.23 and $146.56 emerging as the next major upside levels. Source: Ucan Coin via X

As long as SOL remains above $97.70, the breakout structure stays intact. Losing that support would weaken the near-term momentum and could bring $81.35 back into consideration, making $97.70 the main level separating continuation from a deeper retracement.

Technical View: $146 Comes Into View Above $120

The current Solana price prediction is becoming more constructive as price establishes itself above $100. The first meaningful confirmation now sits around $120, where the daily chart shows the next major horizontal resistance.

A clean break above $120 could open a continuation towards $130-$140 before the larger $146.56 target comes into play. Reaching that level would represent another major step in reversing the broader decline from the 2025 highs.

The downside remains clearly defined. $97.70 is the first major support, while $81.35 represents the stronger lower level if the breakout fails. For now, continued acceptance above $100 keeps the $120-$146 recovery path active.

Bullish Pattern Flags a Long-Term Target

The higher-timeframe Solana price chart also shows a much broader bullish flag forming after the strong expansion from the 2023 lows. Price has spent an extended period moving lower inside a descending channel rather than completely reversing the previous uptrend.

Famous crypto analyst CryptoCurb interprets the structure as a potential continuation pattern, with a breakout from the upper boundary eventually opening a much larger expansion. The chart projects a highly ambitious move above $1,000 if the pattern resolves in the same direction as the preceding rally.

That target remains a long-term and highly speculative scenario rather than an immediate Solana price prediction. Before such levels become technically relevant, SOL would still need to break the flag, recover previous highs around $200-$300 and establish a completely new higher-timeframe expansion.

Solana’s long-term chart shows a large bullish flag, with a highly speculative breakout projection extending beyond $1,000. Source: CryptoCurb via X

Solana and Tokenized Asset Volume

Solana’s growing role in real-world asset markets is adding another dimension to the longer-term outlook. Over the past year, the network reportedly settled $14.7 billion of approximately $46 billion in tokenized asset trading volume, representing roughly 32% of the reported RWA spot volume.

Solana handled approximately $14.7 billion in tokenized asset trading over the past year, representing around 32% of the reported RWA spot volume. Source: Solana via X

Data shared by Solana also shows Backpack generating around $1.5 billion in equity trading volume within two months, while BlackRock and Securitize accounted for approximately $993 million in institutional fixed-income issuance on the network. These figures do not directly determine SOL’s market price, but continued growth in the network could strengthen Solana’s fundamental position if the technical recovery continues.

SOL Technical Analysis Shows $100 as the Main Pivot

Solana’s short-term structure remains constructive while price trades above the $97.70-$100 region. This area now combines psychological support with the previous breakout level, making it the most important zone for bulls to defend.

Solana price trades at $103.47, down 0.19% in the last 24 hours. Source: SOL price via Brave New Coin

Above current price, $105 remains an immediate hurdle before attention moves towards $110 and $120.23. A daily close above $120 would strengthen the broader recovery and expose $130-$140 before $146.56 becomes the next significant target.

On the downside, a loss of $97.70 would weaken the breakout and could send SOL towards the low-$90s. The larger support around $81.35 would become more important if the correction deepens.

Final Thoughts: Solana Conditions Changing?

Solana is showing several signs that the broader market structure may be changing. The first green monthly candle in ten months, an approaching MACD crossover, and the RSI breakout all point towards improving higher-timeframe momentum, while price continues to hold above the $97.70 breakout level.

The next important test is $120.23. Clearing that resistance would strengthen the Solana price prediction and put $146.56 into focus, while continued strength beyond that region could eventually begin challenging the much larger resistance levels left behind during the previous decline.

Fundamentally, Solana’s expanding share of tokenized asset trading provides another positive development to monitor. For now, the outlook remains bullish while $97.70 holds, but a decisive move through $120 would provide stronger confirmation that the current recovery is developing into a broader trend reversal.

summary: Crypto presale activity puts Apeing Stage 3 at $0.0004 in focus as Hyperliquid HYPE nears $90 with record $14.3B open interest.
content:
Skip to content

Crypto presale activity puts Apeing Stage 3 at $0.0004 in focus as Hyperliquid HYPE nears $90 with record $14.3B open interest.

NEW YORK, September 9, 2026 – The crypto presale market has a fresh storyline as Apeing moves into Stage 3 of its live token sale. Named “Paper Hand Panic,” the current phase carries a stated price of $0.0004 for $APEING, alongside a 300 million-token allocation and a project-stated $0.01 listing target. At the same time, Hyperliquid’s HYPE token is trading close to its record level as activity across the decentralized derivatives platform reaches new highs.

The latest crypto news today backdrop shows HYPE around $86.05 after recovering from an intraday low near $81.82. Hyperliquid’s platform-wide open interest has reached a record $14.3 billion, while recurring token burns continue to shape the HYPE narrative. Meanwhile, Apeing is advancing through its 33-stage token sale, creating a contrast between an established trading ecosystem and an early-stage project approaching its next presale phase.

Apeing Pushes Deeper Into Its Stage-Based Crypto Presale

Apeing is now in the third phase of its live crypto presale, known as “Paper Hand Panic.” Instead of offering the entire token allocation at one price, the project has divided its sale into 33 stages, with prices and allocations changing throughout the progression.

The project states that $APEING has a total supply of 16.75 billion tokens, with 40% allocated to the presale. Built on Ethereum using the ERC-20 standard, Apeing combines meme-oriented branding with planned ecosystem features, including staking and referrals. With Stage 3 underway, the project is continuing through its planned roadmap toward a public listing.

“Paper Hand Panic” Creates a New $APEING Entry Point

The current Apeing phase carries a stated price of $0.0004 and includes 300,000,000 tokens. According to the project, the following stage is scheduled at $0.0005, while its planned listing price remains $0.01.

The changing stage prices give the crypto presale a defined progression. Stage 3 establishes the current stated price point, while the next phase introduces another step in the project’s planned pricing structure. This makes the transition between stages an important development for those tracking $APEING.

The 300,000,000-token allocation also gives Stage 3 a specific supply limit. As the phase progresses, attention can shift toward the next stated $0.0005 stage and the broader roadmap leading toward Apeing’s planned listing.

Apeing Staking Adds Another Layer to the Project

The Apeing ecosystem extends beyond the token sale through a multi-level staking concept. The project identifies four categories for participants: Chimp, Monkey, Degen, and Giga Ape.

Reported APYs span from 10% to 85%, with each tier carrying its own participation requirements and reward timelines. This framework gives Apeing another component to its ecosystem strategy, with staking positioned alongside the presale, referral features, and community-building efforts.

Hyperliquid HYPE Nears Its Record as Open Interest Reaches $14.3 Billion

Hyperliquid has emerged as a major established-market story in today’s latest crypto news cycle. HYPE gained roughly 2% during the reported 24-hour period and reached approximately $86.05 after briefly falling toward $81.82. The bigger development is Hyperliquid’s derivatives activity, with platform-wide open interest reaching an all-time high of $14.3 billion, representing a $3.57 billion increase over the previous month. Core perpetual markets have driven much of that expansion.

Hyperliquid’s fee model adds another dimension to the HYPE story. Around 97% of fees from its core perpetual markets are directed toward HYPE buybacks. The protocol recently bought back and burned 15,350 HYPE, valued at approximately $1.32 million, during 24 hours. This activity links platform usage with recurring token purchases and remains a central part of the current HYPE narrative.

The cumulative burn figure has reached 48.45 million HYPE, representing 4.84% of the token’s maximum supply. As Hyperliquid’s trading activity continues to expand, the buyback-and-burn mechanism provides an ongoing tokenomics feature for market participants to monitor alongside HYPE’s price performance and record open-interest levels.

HYPE’s Technical Setup Keeps $100 in View

The latest crypto news today highlights a critical technical test for HYPE. The token has climbed from roughly $52 in early August, accelerated later in the month, moved above the June high near $75, and then challenged its $89 all-time high. Momentum indicators remain constructive, with the daily ADX at 54.58 signaling a strong trend and Chaikin Money Flow positive at 0.15, suggesting continued buying pressure.

HYPE’s immediate resistance sits between $88 and $90. A sustained close above this zone could shift attention toward $95 and potentially the psychological $100 mark, while $82–$83 remains the first major support area and $78–$80 could come into focus during a deeper pullback. On shorter timeframes, HYPE has recovered above its 50-period SMA at $84.75, with the 100-period SMA at $83.23 and the 200-period SMA at $72.15. CCI also recovered to -1.68 after the September 8 correction pushed the indicator into oversold territory.

HYPE’s Buyback Engine Survives a Major Token Unlock

The strength of HYPE is notable given the nearly $820 million token unlock that took place on September 6. Despite the potential for additional supply to create selling pressure, HYPE has remained close to its record level. Recent reporting indicates that only a limited portion of the unlocked HYPE has moved to exchanges, reducing the immediate impact of the distribution. Meanwhile, the protocol’s recurring buyback activity continues to support its tokenomics narrative.

Hyperliquid is also expanding its reach. Since mid-August, Coinbase has directed Base App users toward Hyperliquid, potentially increasing participation in its perpetual markets. The protocol has also explored a potential entry into the regulated U.S. derivatives market through discussions with the CFTC and SEC.

Conclusion

The current market picture places Apeing and HYPE on very different tracks. Hyperliquid has an established trading platform behind it, with HYPE close to its historical peak and open interest at a record $14.3 billion. Apeing, meanwhile, is still progressing through its staged token sale.

Stage 3 puts $APEING at a stated $0.0004, with 300 million tokens assigned to the phase and a stated next-stage price of $0.0005. The project’s planned listing reference remains $0.01, giving the current stage a clear progression point.

That creates two distinct market narratives. HYPE needs to clear the $88–$90 technical barrier to strengthen its path toward $95 and potentially $100. Apeing is focused on completing its current presale phase and moving into the next stage of its planned roadmap.

Frequently Asked Questions About the Crypto Presale

What is a crypto presale?

A crypto presale is an early token sale that allows a project to distribute tokens before a broader public listing or market launch. Presales are commonly structured in stages, with different pricing, allocations, or access conditions as the project progresses.

How do crypto presales work?

Crypto presales typically allow participants to acquire project tokens before they become available on public exchanges. Some projects use multiple stages, with token prices or allocations changing between phases. Buyers should review the project’s terms, tokenomics, roadmap, and risks before participating.

Are crypto presales worth it?

Crypto presales can attract attention because they provide early access to new token projects, but they also carry significant risk. title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, Consensys announced plans to split its MetaMask consumer business from its institutional blockchain operations, Hunter Biden’s LAPTOP memecoin lost most of its value shortly after launch, and Singaporean national Malone Lam pleaded guilty to participating in a crypto theft and money laundering conspiracy involving more than $245 million.

Consensys to split into MetaMask and institutional blockchain company

Consensys Software Inc., the Ethereum software company behind MetaMask, plans to split into two independent companies, separating its consumer business from its institutional blockchain infrastructure operations.

According to Wednesday’s announcement, the separation is expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with Joe Lubin serving as chairman and CEO of MetaMask and executive chairman of the new Consensys.

The new Consensys will house the company’s protocols and institutional infrastructure businesses, including Linea, Besu and Teku, and will be led by CEO Mike Kriak and President David Cunningham. The company will focus on Ethereum infrastructure and helping financial institutions deploy blockchain technology for tokenization, stablecoins and other onchain financial services.

MetaMask will remain focused on consumer self-custody while expanding beyond crypto into payments, savings, investing and traditional financial products.

Hunter Biden’s laptop controversy gets a memecoin afterlife

Hunter Biden’s LAPTOP memecoin fell 95.7% in its first hour of trading on Wednesday, as the son of former US President Joe Biden officially entered the market for politically themed cryptocurrencies.

The token, issued on Ethereum layer-2 network Base, traded at $4.36 at 1:00 pm UTC, after opening at $199.50, according to CoinGecko data. It recorded more than $3 million in trading volume.

“The symbol they used to try to end me is now a symbol of resilience, redemption and recovery,” Biden said in an X post on Wednesday, responding to public backlash.

Biden also said he understood the cynicism around memecoins, called President Donald Trump’s token a “grift” and warned buyers not to expect him or anyone else to make LAPTOP more valuable.

The memecoin is promoted as an attempt to reclaim the “laptop narrative,” which centers on a MacBook that Biden reportedly left at a Delaware repair shop in 2019. The New York Post published emails and other files purported to have come from the device before the 2020 presidential election. Trump allies used the material against Hunter Biden and his father, then-presidential candidate Joe Biden.

Cybercrime ringleader Malone Lam pleads guilty in $245M crypto theft conspiracy

Singaporean national Malone Lam pleaded guilty to participating in a racketeering conspiracy that US prosecutors say used social engineering and home break-ins to steal and launder more than $245 million in cryptocurrency.

On Tuesday, the US Justice Department said that Lam organized the international operation, identified prospective victims and coordinated other conspirators. The enterprise was formed through connections on online gaming platforms and operated from no later than October 2023 through at least May 2025, according to court documents.

The plea establishes criminal responsibility nearly two years after Lam was charged over the theft of more than 4,100 Bitcoin, worth over $230 at the time, from a Washington, DC resident. 

Lam pleaded guilty before US District Judge Colleen Kollar-Kotelly to one count of participating in a Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) conspiracy. The judge scheduled a status hearing for Dec. 8, but the Justice Department did not announce a sentencing date.

title: Zoomex Stock Brings Tesla’s 6% Surge and Nvidia’s Choppy Session Within Reach Through Fair, Rule-Based Derivatives Trading

content:

Founded in 2021, Zoomex is a global cryptocurrency trading platform focused on derivatives trading.

VICTORIA, Seychelles, September 9, 2026 

As Tesla stages one of its sharpest single day moves in months and Nvidia shakes off a volatile session from the day before, Zoomex, the global cryptocurrency derivatives exchange, is once again spotlighting its Stock Perpetuals offering as the venue for traders who want to react to swings like these without the friction of a traditional brokerage account. Built to be Easy to Use from the first click, Zoomex gives retail and professional traders alike a single, unified interface to trade names like TSLA and NVDA, backed by a platform that is Transparent by Design in how positions, margin, and funding are calculated and displayed.

Tesla: Cybercab Launch Fuels a Sharp Rally

Tesla shares have broken well clear of their recent trading pattern today. After spending the past several days confined to a relatively tight band between roughly $350 and $361, the stock jumped more than 6% on Thursday, September 3, climbing to around $378.75 as traders position ahead of the company’s closely watched Cybercab event in Austin, where Tesla is expected to unveil the production version of its two-seat, steering-wheel-free autonomous vehicle.

Source: Zoomex

The move hasn’t stayed confined to Tesla alone, Lucid rose roughly 3%, and Rivian ticked up more modestly, confirming that today’s rally is driven specifically by the Cybercab catalyst rather than a broader sector move. Analysts remain split on what comes next, Morgan Stanley has kept a Hold rating and a $400 price target, warning the stock could “sell off through the event” if Thursday’s presentation lacks concrete production timelines, while StoneX has reiterated a Buy rating with a $475 target tied directly to the Cybercab launch. Beyond the event itself, Tesla reported a rebound in August global deliveries even as Europe remained a soft spot, disclosed a China recall covering roughly three million vehicles over door-handle and driver-monitoring concerns, and pointed to new self-driving data showing a sharp reduction in collision rates versus manually driven cars. Against a 52-week range of $297.38 to $498.83 and a Wall Street consensus price target near $423, the stock remains a magnet for traders positioning around delivery data, regulatory headlines, and Elon Musk’s broader autonomy roadmap.

Nvidia: A Volatile Session Ahead of Tesla’s Big Day

Nvidia had its own turbulent ride heading into Tesla’s headline event. Yesterday, Wednesday, September 2, shares swung through a wide range of roughly $216 to $228 before the session settled near $224, only modestly above where it started the day.

Source: Zoomex

That volatility follows Nvidia’s recent fiscal second-quarter results, which showed revenue up 106% year over year to $96.2 billion and non-GAAP earnings climbing 120% to $2.22 per share, both ahead of analyst expectations. The market is also still digesting news of Nvidia’s $12.93 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, a move read as a deepening bet on the AI software stack, along with an upcoming $0.25 cash dividend carrying a September 10 ex-date. Even with the stock still trading at a discount to the broader Nasdaq-100 on a price-to-earnings basis, analysts including New Street’s Pierre Ferragu see a run past $400 as plausible within eighteen months, while hyperscaler capital spending, projected to climb from roughly $800 billion in 2026 to $1.3 trillion in 2027, continues to anchor the long-term demand story for Nvidia’s data center chips.

Focused on Derivatives: Trading TSLA and NVDA Without Leaving Zoomex

This is precisely the kind of two-sided, headline-driven action that Zoomex Stock Perpetuals were built for. Rather than requiring a traditional equities account, settlement delays, or exposure limited to a single exchange’s trading hours, Zoomex lets users open long or short perpetual contracts referencing TSLA and NVDA directly from their existing derivatives account. The product sits at the center of a platform that is Focused on Derivatives rather than trying to be everything at once, which means the order books, leverage tools, and risk controls traders already use for crypto perpetuals extend naturally to major U.S. equities without forcing anyone to learn a second system.

Fair Access & Rule-Based Execution at the Core of the Product

Fair Access & Rule-Based Execution sits at the core of how Zoomex has designed the Stock Perpetuals product. Every position is filled against clearly published rules rather than discretionary intervention, funding rates and mark-price mechanics are calculated on a fixed, disclosed schedule, and the same execution logic applies whether a trader is sizing into a Tesla position ahead of the Cybercab event or building an Nvidia position around a dividend date. That consistency matters most in exactly the kind of session TSLA and NVDA are having this week, when price can move sharply on a single headline and traders need confidence that the mechanics underneath their trade won’t shift with the market.

A Growing Stock Perpetuals Lineup

Zoomex Stock Perpetuals currently span a growing list of household names alongside TSLA and NVDA, including UnitedHealth, General Electric, JPMorgan, and Gilead, giving traders a single account to express views across technology, healthcare, industrials, and financials without juggling multiple brokers. The addition of two of the most actively traded and news-sensitive stocks in the market, at a moment when Tesla is staging a major product event and Nvidia is still digesting an acquisition and a whipsaw trading session, reflects Zoomex’s broader push to make institutional-grade market access available through a Fair Access & Rule-Based Execution framework that does not discriminate between a first-time trader and an experienced professional.

title: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ‘Strongly Urges’ Senate To Pass Clarity Act
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ‘Strongly Urges’ Senate To Pass Clarity Act
Senators will vote on the long-awaited crypto Clarity Act next week. 
This post US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent ‘Strongly Urges’ Senate To Pass Clarity Act first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is ...
content:
U.S. Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent urged lawmakers to move forward with the crypto Clarity Act when they return from recess next week. 

Writing on X Wednesday, Bessent said that the bill would stop “bad actors” from exploiting important digital asset tech. 

Lawmakers were hoping a crucial vote on the long-awaited crypto market structure bill would go ahead in August before their five-week recess. But it was delayed and the Senate will now vote on it next week. 

“When the Senate returns from August recess, I strongly urge everyone to remain at the negotiating table, agree to the motion to proceed, and continue the legislative process,” he said. 

“Failing to do so would send a troubling signal to our allies and adversaries alike that America is unwilling to lead on the future of digital assets and willing to forgo enhanced national security tools to combat their misuse.”

Just in July, Bessent said lawmakers had to pass the Clarity Act if they wanted to be “on the side of American Exceptionalism” — and quoted Satoshi Nakamoto in another social media post. 

“America will lead or America won’t,” he wrote at the time “It’s not more complicated than that. I believe Satoshi once said it best: ‘If you don’t believe me or don’t get it, I don’t have time to try to convince you, sorry.'”

First passed last year by the House of Representatives, the Clarity Act drafts a framework to formally divide oversight between regulators, distinguishing which digital assets are securities, commodities or stablecoins. 

The digital asset industry has long been calling for such rules to be set in stone. 

But the draft legislation has largely been stalled this year, mostly because the banking lobby clashed with crypto companies over paying customers stablecoin yield. 

A new draft tackling the issue of ethics started circulating in July, banning government officials from promoting or making money from crypto — something Democrats have criticized President Trump’s family for doing. 

Despite the changes, a group of Democrats said the bill fell short and wanted amendments. 

President Donald Trump has urged lawmakers to get the legislation over the line. In August, he said that in order for the U.S. to remain the “undisputed leader in Bitcoin and crypto,” they had to pass the “very, very powerful legislation.”

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Kraken Adds Editable Grid Bot with Backtesting to Desktop App
summary:
Kraken has added Smart Grid, an automated range-trading tool, to its desktop application for eligible Pro users. The exchange is entering a crowded grid-bot category by focusing on backtesting, saved configurations and parameters that can be changed after launch.
Smart Grid is available to eligible ...
content:
2026-09-09T23:02:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 09/09/2026 | 21:02 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Kraken says the bot is not a passive-income product: traders remain responsible for ranges, monitoring, margin and risk settings.
  • The tool lets traders backtest a configuration and change its parameters after the bot has started running.

Kraken has added Smart Grid, an automated range-trading tool, to its desktop application for eligible Pro users. The exchange is entering a crowded grid-bot category by focusing on backtesting, saved configurations and parameters that can be changed after launch.

Smart Grid is available to eligible Kraken Pro users through Kraken Desktop. It runs natively in the desktop application rather than through the exchange’s web interface.

Backtesting Before Capital Goes Live

The bot places a series of buy and sell orders across a price range the trader selects. It is designed to capture price movements within that range without requiring the user to place each order manually.

Before activating the strategy, users can select an eligible trading pair, allocate an investment amount and set the upper and lower price boundaries. They can also choose the number of order levels and the spacing between them. It is also possible to save configurations for reuse or adjust them as market conditions change.

Grid strategies are generally intended for sideways or choppy markets. A sustained move in either direction can take the asset outside the configured range, leaving the strategy unable to continue buying and selling across its intended levels.

To assess that risk, Smart Grid lets traders test chosen parameters against historical price data before committing capital. Backtesting shows how the configuration would have performed previously, but does not predict future results.

Parameters Can Change While the Bot Runs

Kraken lets you edit the grid after activation. Traders can open the configuration panel, change their settings, and apply the revised parameters without stopping the bot or rebuilding the strategy.

The product includes live performance tracking, an overall grid stop-loss, and an option to enable or disable margin. Margin availability and stop-loss behaviour may vary by the user’s account type and region.

Kraken said the bot runs on the same low-latency, low-memory architecture as its native desktop application.

The company is positioning this as an alternative to grid tools running inside browser tabs. The launch follows other 2026 moves aimed at more active and systematic traders.

In April, the exchange promoted its API infrastructure for algorithmic strategies across spot and futures. It subsequently launched Kraken Funded in July, allowing eligible users who pass a trading evaluation to access capital provided by the platform.

According to Kraken's announcement, Smart Grid is not a passive-income product. Users remain responsible for selecting the price range, monitoring the strategy and adjusting its risk settings as market conditions change.

title: Solana Price Prediction: SOL Reclaims Key Moving Averages as Bulls Target a Breakout Toward $116
summary: Solana (SOL) is gaining momentum after reclaiming key moving averages, with bulls now targeting a breakout toward the crucial $116 resistance level.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: SOL

Solana (SOL) is gaining momentum after reclaiming key moving averages, with bulls now targeting a breakout toward the crucial $116 resistance level.

Solana price is finally showing signs of life after months of frustrating price action. Its latest price recovery has brought buyers back into the market, while stronger technical signals and growing interest in SOL investment products are adding to the optimism.

Bullish Crossover Strengthens SOL Momentum

Solana’s broader trend structure is beginning to improve after months of weakness. The latest daily chart shows the SMA-50 turning higher and crossing above the SMA-100 following the sharp recovery from the summer lows.

Known crypto analyst Crypto Rover signals the SMA50-SMA100 crossover as a bullish technical development. The signal has appeared after SOL already reclaimed several important levels, meaning the market is no longer trading in the same declining structure seen earlier in the year.

Maintaining price above $100 while the SMA50 continues moving higher relative to the SMA100 would keep momentum strong and strengthen the possibility of another push towards $110-$116.

Solana has produced a bullish SMA50-SMA100 crossover following its recovery from the summer lows. Source: Crypto Rover via X

Price Targets Point Towards $115-$116

Short-term price action is becoming increasingly compressed around the $104-$106 region. SOL price is trading between rising support and descending resistance, creating a tightening structure that could soon force a larger directional move.

A breakout scenario highlighted by SatoshiOwl places $115-$116 as the next major upside objective. Price first needs to clear the upper boundary around roughly $107-$109, after which the move could accelerate towards $110 and eventually the $115-$116 resistance area.

SOL price is approaching the edge of a tightening technical structure, with $115-$116 highlighted as the next upside target if resistance breaks. Source: SatoshiOwl via X

The same chart also shows why confirmation matters. Failure to break higher could send SOL back towards the lower part of the structure, making $100-$102 the immediate support region to watch. A deeper breakdown would weaken the setup considerably.

SOL’s Base Structure Starts Paying Off

Solana spent several months building a base between approximately $70 and $95 following the larger decline. That range absorbed repeated sell-offs before price finally pushed through its upper boundary and reclaimed $100.

The $70-$95 region acted as a prolonged accumulation range before SOL began its latest expansion higher. Source: Team LAMBO Charts via X

Team LAMBO Charts describes the move as a shift from distribution to accumulation and then expansion. SOL has now broken above the former accumulation zone and is working to hold prices at higher levels.

As long as $95-$100 continues acting as support, the larger breakout remains intact. A sustained expansion from this base could eventually bring $115-$120 into focus, followed by higher resistance zones if momentum continues building.

Solana ETF Inflows Add to the Recovery Setup

Solana spot ETFs recorded approximately $6.18 million in net inflows last week, showing that regulated investment products continue to attract fresh SOL exposure. The size of the inflow remains relatively modest compared with Solana’s overall market capitalization, but the direction is still towards the upside. Positive ETF flows indicate that institutional demand is continuing even as SOL consolidates around the $100 region rather than trading at fresh highs.

For the broader Solana price prediction, sustained ETF inflows could become increasingly relevant if they continue alongside improving technical momentum. Stronger institutional demand combined with a successful breakout above $110 would provide a more convincing backdrop for the larger $115-$120 recovery targets.

Short-Term Technical Analysis

The immediate technical structure revolves around whether SOL can continue defending the $100-$103 region. Price has recovered significantly from its previous range, but the market is now entering resistance around $106-$110.

Solana price trades at $104.00, down 1.39% in the last 24 hours. Source: SOL price via Brave New Coin

A clean move above $110 would strengthen the breakout case and put $115-$116 into focus. Beyond that area, $120 becomes the next psychological target, while a sustained move above $120 could begin opening the way towards $130-$140 over a longer time horizon.

On the downside, losing $100 would weaken the current consolidation and bring $95 back into focus. A deeper move below $95 would represent a more meaningful deterioration because it would return SOL towards the top of its former accumulation range.

Final Thoughts

Solana’s move back above its 50-day and 100-day moving averages has given the recovery a much stronger base. With SOL trading near $104, a clean break from the current triangle could open the next leg towards $110 and $116, while growing interest around Solana ETFs adds another bullish factor to the wider outlook.

The immediate test is whether buyers can defend the $100 area and keep price above the reclaimed moving averages. Holding these levels would keep bulls in a favorable position, but losing them could slow the rally and pull SOL back into consolidation before another breakout attempt.

title: Jack Dorsey’s Block Becomes Latest Bitcoin-Focused Company To Apply for Banking Charter
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Jack Dorsey’s Block Becomes Latest Bitcoin-Focused Company To Apply for Banking Charter
Block wants the banking license so it can open Builders Bank, which would provide custody and related fiduciary services for bitcoin. 
This post Jack Dorsey’s Block Becomes Latest Bitcoin-Focuse...
content:
Bitcoin-focused Block Inc. has become the latest company to apply for a U.S. banking charter. 

The company, which manages Square, Cash App, and Bitkey, said Wednesday that it had submitted an application to the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to establish Builders Bank & Trust, N.A.

Block joins a long-list of digital asset firms that have received conditional approval or are awaiting approval from the regulator to have the license. The charter would allow companies — if fully approved — to have certain banking powers, such as custody assets and move client funds.  

“Building on Block’s experience in the digital asset space, our history with Square Financial Services, and the deep banking expertise of the team we’ve assembled, we believe Builders Bank is well positioned to support Block’s broader vision of economic empowerment,” Lee Woolley, who would serve as President and CEO of Builders Bank, said in a statement. 

Block said that, if approved, Builders Bank would operate as a federally regulated national trust bank under OCC supervision and provide custody and related fiduciary services, including for bitcoin and stablecoins. 

A number of top crypto companies have received conditional approval, including Coinbase, Circle, Crypto.com, and Paxos.

Decentralized financial protocol World Liberty Financial, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, also received approval this year. 

Block CEO and founder Jack Dorsey, a Bitcoin maximalist, has been pushing for the biggest and oldest cryptocurrency to become everyday money. 

His point-of-sale products, Square, last year rolled out bitcoin acceptance for millions of eligible U.S. small businesses, with no setup required and transactions instantly converted to dollars at checkout. 

Mathew Di Salvo

Mathew is a reporter who's covered the space since 2019, reporting on everything from Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele's Bitcoin bet to crypto exchange FTX's bankruptcy.

title: Circle Targets $25B Payments Flow for USDC With $400M Tazapay Deal
summary: Circle is acquiring Tazapay in a $400 million all-stock deal that would bring more than $25 billion in annual payment volume into its orbit. With 60% of Tazapay’s transactions already involving stablecoins, the acquisition could materially expand USDC’s reach across Asia, Africa and other fast-growi...
content:
Circle is acquiring Tazapay in a $400 million all-stock deal that would bring more than $25 billion in annual payment volume into its orbit. With 60% of Tazapay’s transactions already involving stablecoins, the acquisition could materially expand USDC’s reach across Asia, Africa and other fast-growing markets.

Key Takeaways

  • Circle agreed to buy Tazapay for $400M, adding $25B+ in annual payment volume.
  • With 60% of Tazapay volume using stablecoins, USDC could deepen its global payments footprint.
  • Circle still needs regulatory approvals before the deal can close in 2027.

Circle Pushes USDC Into 100+ Markets With Tazapay Acquisition

Circle is making one of its biggest moves yet to push USDC beyond crypto trading and deeper into global commerce.

The stablecoin issuer has agreed to acquire Singapore-based payments infrastructure company Tazapay for $400 million in an all-stock transaction. The deal is expected to close in 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, including clearance from the Monetary Authority of Singapore.

Tazapay brings more than 60 banking and fintech partners, local payout infrastructure across over 100 markets and more than $25 billion in annualized payment volume. The most striking number is that roughly 60% of that volume already involves stablecoins.

Circle Is Buying Distribution, Not Just a Payments Company

For Circle, the transaction offers something difficult to build quickly: banking relationships and local payment rails across fragmented international markets.

“Stablecoin settlement is becoming core infrastructure in the global economy,” Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said in the announcement. He added that combining USDC with Tazapay’s banking network and institutional customer base could accelerate worldwide adoption.

Tazapay has also been a design partner for Circle Payments Network since 2025, meaning the two companies already have an established operating relationship.

Circle senior vice president of payments, Irfan Ganchi, said the acquisition will increase “Circle’s capability to originate and terminate payments globally, near-instant and 24/7, a meaningful step toward making USDC the default payment rail for cross-border commerce.”

That matters because stablecoins solve only part of the cross-border payments problem. Moving USDC globally is easy. Converting it into local currencies and bank accounts across dozens of jurisdictions is much harder.

Asia and Africa Could Be the Bigger Prize

Dragonfly General Partner Rob Hadick called the acquisition “the right move,” pointing to Tazapay’s strength in Asia and the growing importance of Singapore. He also highlighted payment corridors between Asia and Africa as particularly vulnerable to stablecoin disruption because they remain less efficient than mature Western routes.

Tazapay CEO Rahul Shinghal said Circle provides the regulatory standing and dollar infrastructure needed to take the company’s network further.

“Circle has the dollar infrastructure in USDC and the regulatory standing to take what we’ve built further than we could alone,” he said.

Stablecoin Payments Are Entering a New Phase

The deal lands as stablecoin payment activity is accelerating across traditional finance. Visa recently said its stablecoin settlement volume surpassed a $20 billion annualized run rate, up more than 15-fold year over year.

Against that backdrop, Circle is positioning USDC not simply as a crypto asset, but as settlement infrastructure. One commentator, AKA, summarized the thesis more simply on X: “USDC is quietly becoming the internet’s dollar rail.”

The Tazapay acquisition suggests Circle is spending heavily to make that description increasingly literal.

title: DoubleZero adds Kalshi election market data ahead of US midterms
summary: The expansion gives institutional and automated traders real-time access to Kalshi’s political markets as election betting activity continues to grow.
content:
DoubleZero, a network for high-speed data distribution, has added real-time data from Kalshi’s election and politics markets as prediction market trading picks up ahead of the US midterm elections in November.

The expansion adds Kalshi’s election contracts to DoubleZero Edge, which already carries data from the prediction market’s sports contracts and crypto perpetual futures, according to a Wednesday announcement.

The feed includes top-of-book and trade data, along with aggregated order book data from Kalshi’s election markets. Andy Ross, head of institutional at Kalshi, said the integration is intended to make political market data easier to incorporate into institutional workflows as expectations shift around election outcomes.

According to data from the Anti-Corruption Data Collective, betting on the 2026 US midterms had reached $133 million as of Aug. 10, surpassing the $92.4 million wagered during the entire 2024 congressional election cycle.

At the time of writing, a Kalshi midterm market that asks which party will win the US House had recorded more than $35 million in trading volume, with Democratic victory odds at 84%.

Kalshi’s prediction market on which party will win the US House. Source: Kalshi

title: Valutrades Says “Business as Usual” After Pausing Onboarding and Cutting Client Segments
summary:
Valutrades has paused new client onboarding and stopped serving some client segments, but still describes its global operations as “business as usual” and the changes as part of a strategic review of its client portfolio.
The statement came after Finance Magnates reported earlier today that new acco...
content:
2026-09-09T21:47:09.230+02:00

Wednesday, 09/09/2026 | 19:47 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The broker said it stopped serving certain client segments and services that it no longer considers commercially sustainable or profitable.
  • Valutrades did not say when onboarding will resume, which services were affected or which jurisdictions now face closer review.

Valutrades has paused new client onboarding and stopped serving some client segments, but still describes its global operations as “business as usual” and the changes as part of a strategic review of its client portfolio.

The statement came after Finance Magnates reported earlier today that new account applications were unavailable through both the broker’s UK- and Seychelles-regulated entities.

More Selective Client Onboarding

Valutrades is not exiting any market and remains operational across its global footprint, the company said in a press release, seen by Finance Magnates.

New applicants will face tighter screening, especially where clients or jurisdictions carry a higher risk profile.

Valutrades also said it is making “short-term technical changes” to its KYC and onboarding processes, but did not identify the affected services, client categories or jurisdictions.

“We’re concentrating our resources on client segments and markets that are aligned with our long-term business model and that we can serve sustainably,” CEO Graeme Watkins said.

Capital Position Remains Undisclosed

Valutrades also said its financial position remains unchanged and described the business as well-capitalised and supported by its shareholders. It pointed to client funds being held in segregated accounts with Tier 1 banks.

Meanwhile, Valutrades Limited reported a net loss of £671,705 for 2025, an improvement from the £2.59 million loss recorded a year earlier.

Following cumulative losses exceeding £6 million across 2023 and 2024, shareholders provided a further £600,000 capital injection in March 2026.

The company has not disclosed when it will resume onboarding.

title: Grayscale Drives $47M Bitcoin Outflows as XRP Funds Gain $1.55M
summary: U.S. crypto ETFs reopened after the Labor Day break with broad selling pressure, as bitcoin, ether, solana, and HYPE funds all posted net outflows. XRP ETFs were the only major category to finish Tuesday in positive territory, drawing $1.55 million. Crypto ETFs Open Short Week With Multiple Selloffs...
content:
U.S. crypto ETFs reopened after the Labor Day break with broad selling pressure, as bitcoin, ether, solana, and HYPE funds all posted net outflows. XRP ETFs were the only major category to finish Tuesday in positive territory, drawing $1.55 million.

Key Takeaways

  • U.S. bitcoin ETFs lost $46.65M on Tuesday, while XRP funds alone posted $1.55M in inflows.
  • Broad ETF outflows signaled reduced crypto risk appetite after last week’s stronger institutional demand.
  • Investors will watch whether the rest of the week produces a bounce back to inflows.

Crypto ETFs Open Short Week With Multiple Selloffs

The first session after the Labor Day holiday brought little appetite for risk across the crypto exchange-traded fund (ETF) market.

Bitcoin ETFs recorded $46.65 million in net outflows, even as several major funds attracted fresh capital. Bitwise’s BITB added $14.47 million, Blackrock’s IBIT brought in $10.66 million, Ark & 21Shares’ ARKB gained $8.06 million, and Morgan Stanley’s MSBT added $7.41 million.

Those inflows were overwhelmed by redemptions elsewhere. Grayscale’s GBTC lost $65.51 million, Fidelity’s FBTC shed $17.05 million, and Invesco’s BTCO posted a $4.68 million outflow.

Daily trading value reached $2.41 billion, while net assets closed at $99.52 billion. The flows add another layer of pressure for traders watching the correlation between ETF flows and bitcoin’s price after last week’s strong institutional demand.

Ether Funds Join the Pullback

Ether ETFs also finished lower, posting $24.29 million in net outflows.

Grayscale’s Ether Mini Trust lost $24.61 million, while ETHE recorded another $9.57 million exit. Fidelity’s FETH attracted $9.89 million, helping soften the overall decline. Trading activity across ether ETFs reached $952.22 million. Net assets closed at $15.72 billion.

The session marked a quieter start to the week for the broader crypto market after the strong inflow momentum seen in recent sessions.

XRP Holds up as Solana and HYPE Weaken

XRP ETFs were the day’s only gainers, attracting $1.55 million. The entire inflow went into Franklin’s XRPZ. Trading value reached $36.21 million, while net assets ended at $1.51 billion. The positive flow offers a modest sentiment signal for investors tracking XRP’s price.

HYPE ETFs recorded $12.96 million in outflows. Bitwise’s BHYP lost $8.06 million, while 21Shares’ THYP shed $4.89 million, with net assets closing at $464.06 million.

Solana ETFs slipped by $667,720. A $502,730 inflow into 21Shares’ TSOL was offset by a $1.17 million exit from Grayscale’s GSOL. Net assets finished at $1.43 billion.

TRX Joins the US ETF Market

Tuesday also brought a new addition to the digital-asset ETF market.

The first U.S.-listed TRX ETF debuted on Cboe under the ticker TRXS. Its staking rewards will be reinvested into the fund rather than distributed as cash.

For now, however, bitcoin remains the main institutional barometer. Tuesday’s flows showed a softer opening to the week, with capital turning selective across the major crypto ETF categories.

title: B2PRIME Q2 Net Profit Jumps 79% Amid Gold and Oil Volatility
summary:
B2PRIME says its infrastructure helped turn volatile trading conditions into higher profit in the second quarter. However, its update does not separate the effect of technology investments from increased market activity.


Volatility Replaces the Summer Slowdown


B2PRIME said the expected summer sl...
content:
2026-09-09T20:51:00.000+02:00

Wednesday, 09/09/2026 | 18:51 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Operating profit increased 74% between the first and second quarters.
  • H1 trading income reached €56.5 million, exceeding the total for 2025.

B2PRIME says its infrastructure helped turn volatile trading conditions into higher profit in the second quarter. However, its update does not separate the effect of technology investments from increased market activity.

The company reported the figures in a leadership letter rather than a full set of financial statements.

Volatility Replaces the Summer Slowdown

B2PRIME said the expected summer slowdown did not materialise as geopolitical tensions instead contributed to sharp movements in commodity markets, particularly oil and gold.

For a liquidity and trading infrastructure provider, that environment works in two directions. Greater volatility can generate additional trading opportunities and client activity, but it also increases demands on execution quality and system reliability.

Against this backdrop, B2PRIME’s net profit rose 79% between Q1 and Q2 2026. Operating profit increased 74% over the same period, and the company cited this as evidence that the improvement came from its core trading business rather than one-off items.

The firm did not disclose the quarterly profit amounts. Based on the previously reported, rounded 2025 profit of €15 million, this implies roughly €20 million for H1 2026.

Applying the disclosed quarterly growth rate would suggest about €7 million in Q1 and €13 million in Q2, though B2PRIME did not publish those figures. These are derived figures, not amounts published by B2PRIME.

Trading Income Passes the 2025 Total

Client trading income reached €56.5 million during the first six months of 2026. That was about 7% above the €52.8 million generated throughout 2025, when the figure rose 165% year-on-year and gold accounted for much of the growth, as Finance Magnates previously reported.

B2PRIME linked its latest performance to earlier infrastructure spending. The company has set a goal of becoming an “AI-native brokerage” and announced an AI Assistant for B2TRADER in June.

The tool places forecasts, sentiment analysis and other market context inside the trading workspace. After its June rollout, it extended access to guests.

The quarter also included a redesigned client interface and the opening of an expanded Cyprus office. Shareholder equity increased 54%, though B2PRIME did not disclose the absolute value.

The comparison between H1 2026 and the whole of 2025 shows the recent acceleration. Without exact profit amounts or an H1 2025 comparison, however, the update does not establish the year-on-year growth rate or show how much of the result reflects seasonal trading conditions.

title: Consensys to split into MetaMask and institutional blockchain company
summary: The restructuring will separate MetaMask’s consumer business from Consensys’ Ethereum protocols and institutional blockchain infrastructure operations.
content:
Consensys Software Inc., the Ethereum software company behind MetaMask, plans to split into two independent companies, separating its consumer business from its institutional blockchain infrastructure operations.

According to Wednesday’s announcement, the separation is expected to be completed by the end of 2026, with Joe Lubin serving as chairman and CEO of MetaMask and executive chairman of the new Consensys.

The new Consensys will house the company’s protocols and institutional infrastructure businesses, including Linea, Besu and Teku, and will be led by CEO Mike Kriak and President David Cunningham. The company will focus on Ethereum infrastructure and helping financial institutions deploy blockchain technology for tokenization, stablecoins and other onchain financial services.

MetaMask will remain focused on consumer self-custody while expanding beyond crypto into payments, savings, investing and traditional financial products.

Source: MetaMask

MetaMask has recorded more than 100 million downloads across roughly 190 countries and facilitated trillions of dollars in transaction volume, according to the company.

The company said the restructuring reflects increasingly different priorities for its consumer and institutional businesses.

Related: Ethereum Foundation names 2 ‘must ship’ EIPs for Hegotá upgrade

MetaMask’s evolution beyond crypto wallet

MetaMask, which launched in 2016 as an Ethereum browser extension for accessing decentralized applications and managing crypto assets, has expanded beyond those roots over the past year, adding products spanning payments, yield and tokenized traditional assets.

In June, MetaMask launched Money Account, which allows users to earn up to 4% variable APY on eligible mUSD stablecoin balances and spend the funds through MetaMask Card. The yield is generated through DeFi lending strategies rather than interest paid by MetaMask or the stablecoin issuer.

Source: MetaMask

In February, the company added access to 200 tokenized US stocks, exchange-traded funds and commodities through Ondo Global Markets for eligible users outside the United States.

Later that month, it rolled out its Mastercard-enabled spending card across 49 US states, expanding a product previously available in markets including Europe, Canada, Mexico, Brazil and Argentina.
